_comment: Regeneration record for the Stoa agent-card character images. Pairs each VERBATIM image-generation prompt with its output file and the OpenAI session that produced it, so the full set can be redone if a file is lost or a restyle is wanted. Human-readable companion lives at docs/agent-cards/prompts.md (condensed); this manifest is the authoritative verbatim source.
author: Denson Smith

source.note: Shared ChatGPT session that generated the period + future sheets. Provenance only — open it to inspect or redo.

image_path_scheme: docs/agent-cards/images/<id>/<look>-<sheet>.png   (look: period|future; sheet: turnaround|expressions). Majors carry an expressions sheet; captains carry turnaround only. The grid card crops to the rightmost (close-up) panel of the turnaround.
style_block: World of Warcraft–style semi-realistic painterly heroic-fantasy character render, Blizzard-cinematic high detail (believable worn materials, ornate but grounded, dramatic light) — NOT cartoony or cel-shaded. 4-panel character turnaround sheet (front, 3/4, side profile, head-and-shoulders close-up), the SAME character identical across every panel, neutral studio backdrop, name hand-lettered across the top.
workflow: Generate the period sheet first; then attach that sheet back in as the reference image for the matching future sheet so the face stays identical. Each future-sheet entry names its required reference in the 'reference' field.
priority_order: then nomos, strabo, bartleby, herald, curator, zeno, tiro as gold-plating

agents.name: POLYBIUS
agents.history: Polybius (c. 200–118 BC), Greek statesman and historian. His Histories traced Rome's rise with rigorous, source-checked "pragmatic history." → keeps the record, sees the whole board.
agents.character_constant: authoritative Greek man ~60, silver-grey hair and a short well-kept beard, keen analytical eyes, calm commanding bearing.

Character: an authoritative Greek man of ~60, silver-grey hair and a short well-kept beard, keen analytical eyes, calm commanding bearing. Authentic Hellenistic-Greek statesman's dress (2nd c. BC): a heavy wool himation draped over a linen chiton, leather sandals, a bronze signet ring; he carries rolled papyrus scrolls.
